> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b7fb116b2293dc0756cab9ed6e6a7652d2893768` — the merge of head `0df297be078c9575aeddc013b7064f9453efa90e` into base `b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b7fb116b2293dc0756cab9ed6e6a7652d2893768 && git checkout b7fb116b2293dc0756cab9ed6e6a7652d2893768
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834 0df297be078c9575aeddc013b7064f9453efa90e && git checkout -B drift-repro b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834 && git merge --no-ff 0df297be078c9575aeddc013b7064f9453efa90e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b12e16a561cae3da15c09b463b470ce760b11834` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT

`domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_01SYEJqDL3NXxrJRBVqaMu9T` · 2026-10-19T18:58Z · on head `69778e478` · #24567 row 3 (p1 + `target:v18`, claim `6273418995`, report `6274807854`). This is the seat's own review at the default tier, read against the diff on GitHub, not the report.

1. **What moved, read on the compare `65a8eeb7d...69778e478`:**
   - **`apply.ts`'s drop-gate refusal (both unverified branches) and its `--json` `detail`** name no step of `os migrate organization-ownership`. They now say: "18.0 supports fresh installs only and does not upgrade a v17 database: keep a v17 database on a 17.x release until the 18.x release that carries the upgrade path, whose ceremony drops these columns itself". That is the boot refusal's position. The verified-marker branch, where the drop may proceed, is kept.
   - **The registered 18.0 `organization-ownership` command's `--help`** shows its refusal (two examples). The ceremony class keeps its six examples for the 18.x release that registers it.
   - **`os dev`'s way-on line** (`utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts`) is fixed the same way. It was within the claim's census line.
   - Message code, `tables`, `marker`, exit code and every flag are unchanged.
2. **The seat's hypothesis was corrected by measurement.** The claim assumed a fresh 18.0 install supports `organization-ownership --apply`. It does not: the registered command refuses plan and apply on every database. So no branch of the old text was true anywhere in 18.0, and changing both refused branches is right.
3. **Shape:**
   - `Fixes #24567`, a line-initial `Clause-②: no` (text only), and a `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/cli`.
   - 8 files, +276 / −12. Not governed.
   - `packages/runtime/**` and `packages/spec/**` are untouched (hold-offs kept).
4. **Proof:**
   - Through the real CLI on a 17.x-shaped SQLite: before, the refusal prescribed `--out PLAN` / `--apply --plan-file PLAN`, and running that answered `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. After, the text above. Exit 1 at both; the column is kept.
   - The new `apply.organization-ownership-refusal.test.ts` passes 5/5. An ablation restoring the old prescription reds the 2 human-face cases (the `--json` and control cases read `detail` and the writes). The restore was proven by blob.
   - The cli unit tier passes 314 files (4,640 tests), the edited integration file 5/5, and typecheck exits 0.
5. **Gates:** `dispatch-gates` ran 68 derived and 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. The 11 declared-wide families and the full-union `pnpm lint` exited 0. Landing waits on every check of this head.
6. **Findings:**
   - **Filed #24637**: the family close-out. The same withdrawn-command prescription remains in spec's ADR-0087 upgrade-guide entries (`domain:spec`), the runtime boot guard's unverified and read-failure branches (`domain:cli`), plugin-security's catalog reference report (`domain:services`), and four hand-written docs pages (`domain:devx`). It is filed under the release-text exception, with this PR as the landed member. The dev's docs-drift note is folded into its `domain:devx` row.
   - **Filed #24638**: the dev's open question, as a decision card. A database 18.0 created whose object newly declares `systemFields: { tenant: false }` has no way on in 18.0. It sits outside ruling `6259608309`'s v17 scope. The seat recommends A (text only).
   - `dev.ts:822` still prints "upgrading it in place" before a refusal; it names no command. Acceptance notes.
7. **Landing:** ready plus auto-merge through the queue once every check of `69778e478` is green or a rostered skip. It is not a narrowing, so no contract review is owed. The card closes on the merge.

## 席位核对 — REWORK (patch round 1: one integration pin still reads the old `detail`)

`domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_01SYEJqDL3NXxrJRBVqaMu9T` · 2026-10-19T19:13Z · on head `69778e478` · #24567 row 3 (claim `6273418995`, report `6274807854`). ACCEPT `6274910235` stands on everything but this.

**What is red:** `Test Core (3/6)` and `Test Core` on `69778e478` (job `118243279742`).
- `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-platform-global-column-drop.integration.test.ts:439` still asserts `expect(payload.detail).toMatch(/os migrate organization-ownership --apply/)`.
- The run received `"No run of the organization-ownership ceremony is recorded on this database."`, which is exactly the `detail` this PR rewrote.
- The test is "holds the drop back until the marker is verified, naming the ceremony, and drops nothing": 1 failed | 1,894 passed in `@objectstack/cli`.
- This is this PR's own change, not a flake.

**Why it was missed:** the run read the unit tier in full but only the integration file it edited. The seat's census over `packages/cli`'s tests for assertions on the old prescription (`toMatch` / `toContain` of `organization-ownership --apply|--out`, or `plan-file PLAN`) finds two on `origin/main`:
- `apply-organization-ownership-gate.integration.test.ts:154`, which this PR already edits;
- `organization-ownership-platform-global-column-drop.integration.test.ts:439`, the red one.

**Owed in this round:**
1. Re-point `:439` to the new `detail`. Assert what the refusal now says, and that it names no withdrawn step, as in the edited `:154`.
2. Re-run the census over every test file in `packages/cli` (unit and integration) for any other assertion on the removed wording, and fix what it finds.
3. Run `@objectstack/cli`'s **integration** project in full locally (`--project integration`), in addition to the unit tier, under the verify lock. Quote the totals.
4. ⛔ Do not patch the PR body. Give exact old/new pairs for the Verification section, so it states the integration run; the seat writes them.
